claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children do you have, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I have one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child named Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details about your circumstances. Let me start with the first question:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 21 years old - he was born in March 2003.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to let you know that based on Alex's age, this may affect eligibility, but let me gather a bit more information to give you a complete assessment.

**Are you currently the person responsible for Alex, and is Alex living with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

Now, I need to ask about your residency status, as this is an important factor for Child Benefit eligibility:

**What is your residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, settled in the UK, or do you have another immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen and I live here in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have one more important question to ask:

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training, such as a school, college, or a recognised apprenticeship programme?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not studying anymore. He finished his A-levels a few years ago and now he's working full-time at a warehouse.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 21 years old (born in March 2003)
- Alex lives with you
- You are a British citizen living in Manchester
- Alex is not in full-time education or approved training
- Alex is working full-time

Unfortunately, Child Benefit is only payable for children who are under 16 years old, or under 19 if they are in full-time education or approved training. Since Alex is 21 and not in education or training, he falls outside the age eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. 

The key reason is that Alex is 21 years old and no longer in full-time education or training. Child Benefit eligibility requirements are:
- Children under 16 automatically qualify, or
- Young people aged 16-18 who are in full-time education or approved training

Since Alex is 21 and working full-time rather than studying, he falls outside these eligibility criteria.

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit or your circumstances change in the future, feel free to ask!
